title: China’s CXMT surges almost 500% in Shanghai debut, tops Intel in market value
summary: Shares of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT jumped 465.8% in their Shanghai debut, valuing the company at over 3.6 trillion yuan and briefly surpassing Intel and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China. The IPO raised 57.92 billion yuan and highlights strong investor appetite for semiconductors as China pushes for chip self-sufficiency amid U.S. export limits and booming AI demand.
content:
Stocks end mixed to kick off key week dominated by mega-cap earnings, Fed decision

BofA names top semiconductor stocks to buy after sector selloff

SpaceX bears should ’consider cryogenic hibernation’ on ship catch: Morgan Stanley

Oil prices tumble after U.S. and Iran pause fighting, Brent falls below $90

© Reuters.

Investing.com-- Shares of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT Corp (688825.SS) closed 465.8% in their Shanghai stock market debut on Monday, propelling the company to become China’s most valuable listed firm, and lifting its market capitalization above that of U.S. chipmaker Intel (NASDAQ:INTC).

The rally valued the company at more than 3.6 trillion yuan (about $530 billion), surpassing Intel’s market capitalization and overtaking Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (SS:601398) as the country’s largest listed company by value.

CXMT, China’s leading DRAM memory chipmaker, raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in the listing, with proceeds earmarked to expand production capacity, fund research and development, and strengthen working capital. The offering was Asia’s largest IPO of 2026.

The blockbuster debut underscores strong investor appetite for semiconductor stocks as China accelerates efforts to achieve self-sufficiency in advanced chipmaking amid ongoing U.S. export restrictions and booming demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The company has emerged as a key beneficiary of surging demand for memory chips used in AI servers and data centers.

Recent media reports showed that Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) was seeking approval from the Trump administration to use memory chips supplied by CXMT in devices sold outside the U.S. as it looks to diversify its supply chain amid a global memory shortage.

The sizable first-day gain and enormous valuation reflect both investor enthusiasm for semiconductor plays tied to AI and broader strategic support inside China for homegrown chipmakers. CXMT’s proceeds will be directed at scaling production and R&D to meet accelerating demand.

(Reporting by Investing.com; © Reuters.)

## IPO debut and valuation

Investing.com-- Shares of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT Corp (688825.SS) closed 465.8% in their Shanghai stock market debut on Monday, propelling the company to become China’s most valuable listed firm, and lifting its market capitalization above that of U.S. chipmaker Intel (NASDAQ:INTC).

## Market value and ranking

The rally valued the company at more than 3.6 trillion yuan (about $530 billion), surpassing Intel’s market capitalization and overtaking Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (SS:601398) as the country’s largest listed company by value.

## Use of proceeds

CXMT, China’s leading DRAM memory chipmaker, raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in the listing, with proceeds earmarked to expand production capacity, fund research and development, and strengthen working capital. The offering was Asia’s largest IPO of 2026.

## Investor interest and context

The blockbuster debut underscores strong investor appetite for semiconductor stocks as China accelerates efforts to achieve self-sufficiency in advanced chipmaking amid ongoing U.S. export restrictions and booming demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

## Demand drivers

The company has emerged as a key beneficiary of surging demand for memory chips used in AI servers and data centers.

## Apple supply-chain report

Recent media reports showed that Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) was seeking approval from the Trump administration to use memory chips supplied by CXMT in devices sold outside the U.S. as it looks to diversify its supply chain amid a global memory shortage.

## Analysis

The sizable first-day gain and enormous valuation reflect both investor enthusiasm for semiconductor plays tied to AI and broader strategic support inside China for homegrown chipmakers. CXMT’s proceeds will be directed at scaling production and R&D to meet accelerating demand.
